body.statement: For \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), and sufficiently small fixed \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{diag}}\), every \(P_{0,\sigma,\ell}\) and \(P_{1,\ell}\) from def:rough-prior-diagnostic belongs to \(\mathcal P(1/10,1/10,1,L,1)\), every null component obeys \(\tau_{0,\sigma}\equiv1/8\), and averaging \(P_{0,\sigma,\ell}\) over \(\sigma\) exactly matches the one-observation law of \(P_{1,\ell}\). The first nonmatching repeated-observation likelihood moment is order two: conditional on \(X_i=x,X_k=z\), the null-mixture covariance \(\operatorname{Cov}(A_i,A_k\mid X_i=x,X_k=z)\) equals \(q_{\ell}^2\sum_{j=1}^{M_{\mathrm{diag}}}b_{j,\ell}(x)b_{j,\ell}(z)\), whereas it is zero under \(P_{1,\ell}^{\otimes2}\). Moreover \(D(P_{1,\ell})=4\epsilon_{\mathrm{diag}}^2\ell\{\tfrac12\int_0^1b(t)^4dt-\tfrac14(\int_0^1b(t)^2dt)^2\}^{1/2}>0\).
body.justification: The rough symmetric case now has an explicit legal early-kill calculation rather than a promissory appeal to moment matching.
body.gap: The one-observation equality does not furnish a converse because shared local signs leak through the displayed two-observation moment; matching or suppressing that term at the sharp rough-nuisance scale remains open.
body.consumer: The proposition determines the first moment that every candidate fixed-sample lower prior must neutralize before its divergence calculation is credible.
